draft.title: What a force is
card: A force is a push or a pull on an object. Kicking a ball is a push. Pulling open a door is a pull.
Force is measured in newtons, written N. A force meter (also called a spring balance) measures it.
A force arrow shows a force in a diagram. The arrow starts on the object.
The length of the arrow shows the size of the force. The direction the arrow points shows the direction of the force.
draft.remember: A force is a push or a pull. Its size is in newtons, and its arrow shows size and direction.

a.q: Which of these is an example of a force?
opts: A child pulling a wagon along a path
A wagon that is painted red
A wagon that is 80 cm long
A wagon sitting in a shed
a.why: Pulling the wagon is a pull, so it is a force. Colour and length describe the wagon but do not push or pull it. A wagon sitting in a shed is not an example of a push or pull.
a.clue: Look for a push or a pull.

b.q: Sam draws two force arrows on a diagram. Arrow X is 4 cm long and arrow Y is 2 cm long, and both point right. What does this show?
opts: The force for X is bigger than for Y, in the same direction
The force for Y is bigger than for X, in the same direction
The forces are equal, but X acts for a longer time
The forces are equal in size, but point in opposite ways
b.why: Arrow length shows the size of a force, so the longer arrow X is the bigger force. Both arrows point right, so both forces act in the same direction. The direction is shown by where the arrow points, not by its length.
b.clue: Length shows size, and the point shows direction.

a.best: A child pulling a wagon along a path

b.best: The force for X is bigger than for Y, in the same direction

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one that describes an action. It also uses the word 'pulling', which matches the clue 'Look for a push or a pull', so a student can pick it by matching words without understanding the idea.

The why says a wagon sitting in a shed 'is not an example of a push or pull'. This could suggest to students that no forces act on a still object. In fact gravity and the floor's support act on it as balanced forces (point 2), so the why should say only that the option does not describe a push or pull being applied.

proposal.title: What a force is
card: A force is a push or a pull on an object. Kicking a ball is a push. Pulling open a door is a pull.
A force is not the same as movement. The ball rolling away after the kick is its motion, not a force.
Force is measured in newtons, written N. A force meter (also called a spring balance) measures it.
A force arrow shows a force in a diagram. It starts on the object. Its length shows the size of the force, and where it points shows the direction.
proposal.remember: A force is a push or a pull. Its size is in newtons, and its arrow shows size and direction.

a.q: Which of these is a force acting on a shopping trolley?
opts: A shopper pushing the trolley along an aisle
The trolley rolling along an aisle on its own
The trolley moving quickly along an aisle
The trolley travelling 10 metres along an aisle
a.why: The shopper's push acts on the trolley, so it is a force. Rolling, moving quickly and travelling 10 metres describe how the trolley moves. Movement is not a push or a pull being applied.
a.clue: Is something acting on the trolley, or is it only moving?
